Directory Description: Funky Elephant is a chef-owned Thai spot in West Berkeley's Gilman District, opened by Supasit Puttikaew, formerly chef de cuisine at Oakland's Hawker Fare, and partner Nanchaphon Laptanachai. The kitchen calls its cooking non-traditional Thai comfort food and makes its curry pastes by hand. Regulars come for khao mun gai (poached chicken and rice), a crispy rice salad with house-made nham moo sausage, fiery pad Thai, Thai-spicy wings and fried Brussels sprouts. It has earned Michelin Guide recognition and a spot on Eater's list of Berkeley's best restaurants.
Highlights: Khao mun gai; crispy rice salad with house-made nham moo; pad Thai; Thai-spicy party wings; fried Brussels sprouts; handmade curry pastes
Notes to Verify: Opened about 2017-2018 per press dates on its site. Shares the 1313 Ninth St building with Homeroom (already in your list). Phone from Eater.

Cuisine: Korean American; breakfast, brunch and dinner; full bar
Directory Description: Berkeley Social Club is a big, group-friendly Korean American restaurant on University Avenue with something for almost everyone. Mornings bring Korean-accented brunch plates such as a bulgogi scramble and a Korean fried chicken benedict with gochujang hollandaise, along with mascarpone crunch French toast. Later in the day the menu turns to shareable dishes like army stew, a spicy seafood dolsot, takoballs and poke noodles. There's a full bar with beer and cocktails and a heated back patio for eating outdoors.
Highlights: Bulgogi scramble; Korean F.C. Benedict; mascarpone crunch French toast; BSC army stew; spicy seafood dolsot; takoballs; full bar; heated back patio
Notes to Verify: Owners not identified in any source reached. Hours not published on the website (site is set to noindex). Confirm hours, ownership and that it is independently owned.

Cuisine: Bagels, coffee and all-day wine bar
Directory Description: Cafe Brusco is the all-day sister to Rose Pizzeria, run by owners Gerad Gobel and Alexis Rorabaugh on University Avenue. Mornings center on specialty coffee and creative bagels, and diners can mix and match bagel halves to try more than one. Favorites include the Sneaky Persimmon, with thin fuyu persimmon, sumac and basil, and the Brusco, layered with pistachio mortadella, honey and Calabrian cream cheese. As the day goes on it becomes a relaxed wine bar with natural wines by the glass or bottle to take home.
Highlights: Mix-and-match bagel halves; Sneaky Persimmon bagel; Brusco (pistachio mortadella, honey, Calabrian cream cheese); specialty coffee; natural wine; bottle shop
Notes to Verify: No phone or hours on the website text Firecrawl could read. Opened about late 2025 (Eater review Dec 2025).

Directory Description: Rose Pizzeria makes thin-crust pies with thoughtful ingredients and old-school flavor on University Avenue, from owners Gerad Gobel and Alexis Rorabaugh. The champione pizza, with spring onion cream, roasted mushrooms, mozzarella and green onions, is a house favorite, and the blistered crust is the draw. Pair it with the spicy Caesar and save room for tiramisu. There's indoor seating and a patio, plus takeout and online reservations. The owners also run Cafe Brusco nearby and a second Rose Pizzeria in San Francisco.
Highlights: Champione pizza; spicy Caesar salad; tiramisu; wine; patio; reservations and takeout
Notes to Verify: Website says 'no phone'; phone shown is from Eater. Owner names from Eater's Cafe Brusco entry. Has a second location at 1 Clement St, San Francisco.

Directory Description: Ippuku brings a slice of Tokyo to downtown Berkeley. The intimate room is lined with wood and has low, shoes-off tatami-style tables, and it's one of the Bay Area's go-to spots for yakitori. Specialty chicken cuts are grilled over charcoal, from thigh 'oyster' and neck to breast rolled with shiso and salted plum. Other small plates include panko-fried oysters and yuba tofu skin with ankake sauce. A deep list of sake, shochu and Japanese beer rounds out the experience, and the Michelin Guide has awarded it a Bib Gourmand.
Highlights: Yakitori specialty cuts; breast with shiso and ume; panko-breaded oysters; yuba with ankake; sake and shochu list; tatami seating; Michelin Bib Gourmand
Notes to Verify: PHONE CONFLICT: Eater lists (510) 665-1969; Michelin lists (510) 655-1969. Owner not named in sources reached.

Address: 2054 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley, CA 94702 (cafe at 2056 San Pablo Ave)
Directory Description: Middle East Market is a long-running Persian grocery on San Pablo Avenue whose kitchen is one of Berkeley's best-kept secrets. Owner Razavi, a regular customer since moving to Berkeley from Yazd in 1976, now runs the store, which in late 2025 added a cafe next door. The kitchen turns out well-charred koobideh kebabs, tender lamb shanks and herb-heavy stews like ghormeh sabzi. Before leaving, pick up a bag of Persian flatbread and some sweets from the well-stocked shelves.
Highlights: Koobideh kebab; lamb shank; ghormeh sabzi; Persian flatbread; Persian pastries and sweets; full grocery
Notes to Verify: Owner's first name not captured (Oaklandside refers to him as Razavi). Cafe opened Nov 2025 at 2056 San Pablo.

Directory Description: Great China is a Berkeley institution for family and group dinners, set in a chic dining room on Bancroft Way near campus. Its signature is the 'double skin,' a cold platter of mung bean sheets, egg crepe, seafood, mushrooms and pork tossed together at the table. The Peking duck, carved and served with pancakes, plum sauce and scallions, is the other must-order and is best reserved ahead. The restaurant also has an unusually deep wine list, including a strong run of Burgundies, and holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Highlights: Double skin; Peking duck; extensive wine list with Burgundies; Michelin Bib Gourmand; good for groups
Hours: Lunch Sat-Sun 11:30am-2:30pm; dinner Mon, Wed, Thu 5-8:30pm (Fri-Sun later); closed Tue (per website/Yelp)
Notes to Verify: Family-run for decades per general knowledge, but owner names not captured from a source. Confirm Fri-Sun dinner hours.

Directory Description: Vik's Chaat began in 1989 as a small corner of Vik's warehouse retail store in West Berkeley, and it grew so popular that it expanded in 2004 into the bustling, cafeteria-style hall it is today. It serves more than 2,000 dishes a day to crowds of families and friends. Nearly every table orders chole bhature, the giant puffed bread with chickpea curry, and the rest of the chaat menu, from pani puri to kathi rolls, is reliably good. The adjoining Vik's Market is the place to stock up on Indian pantry staples.
Highlights: Chole bhature; pani puri; kathi rolls; wide chaat menu; adjoining Vik's Market; indoor and patio seating
Notes to Verify: Family-owned business; owner names not captured.

Directory Description: Cafe Bolita is chef-owner Emmanuel Galvan's tribute to masa, opened in spring 2026 by the founder of Bolita Masa. Built around heirloom corn, the daytime menu includes hand-rolled tortillas filled with Rancho Gordo pinto beans and Oaxacan quesillo, and tostadas topped with whatever produce is in season. Occasional specials like caldo de pollo with chochoyotes show off the kitchen's range. Arrive after 11am when the menu expands to heartier dishes. Evenings sometimes bring pop-up collaborations.
Highlights: Heirloom corn masa; hand-rolled tortillas with Rancho Gordo beans and quesillo; seasonal tostadas; caldo de pollo con chochoyotes (special); evening pop-ups
Hours: Wed-Sat, breakfast and lunch (opens 9am; fuller menu from 11am)
Notes to Verify: New (grand opening March 25, 2026). No phone found. Confirm exact closing time.

Directory Description: State Flour Pizza Company is the Elmwood pizzeria of PizzaHacker alum Derek Lau, who has been baking here since 2022. The menu spans thinner New York-leaning pies and thick, bready Sicilian squares, with classics like pepperoni and margherita. The weekly special is the one to watch, often built around seasonal produce, such as corn, pepperoni, jalapeño and aji verde. Slices are sold at lunch, Mondays bring a calzone special, and there's a gluten-free pan pizza.
Highlights: Weekly seasonal special pie; Sicilian squares; pizza by the slice at lunch; Monday calzone special; gluten-free pan pizza
Notes to Verify: No phone found (it had none at 2022 opening). Hours not confirmed.

Directory Description: Lemat is a warm, family-run Ethiopian restaurant on Adeline Street. Owner Gezu Mengistu runs it with his wife, Ejigayehu, while her sister Tigist Gelan leads the kitchen. It's known for tender, buttery kitfo, tangy injera made entirely from teff, and a generous vegetarian combination platter, with gluten-free and vegan-friendly options throughout. Finish with a traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony.
Highlights: Kitfo; 100% teff injera (gluten-free); veggie combo; vegan options; Ethiopian coffee ceremony
Hours: Opens 5pm Mon (per Yelp); full weekly hours not confirmed
Notes to Verify: Owner info from a 2018 Berkeleyside story; confirm current. Confirm full hours.

Directory Description: Comal has been a downtown Berkeley favorite since 2012, when owner John Paluska opened it on Shattuck Avenue. The lively restaurant draws on the flavors of Oaxaca and other regions of Mexico, with shareable plates, wood-grilled meats and seafood, and handmade tortillas. A big bar pours margaritas and a deep list of mezcal and tequila, and the back patio is one of the nicer outdoor spots downtown. It holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Highlights: Shareable Mexican plates; handmade tortillas; wood-fired grill; mezcal and tequila list; back patio; Michelin Bib Gourmand
Hours: Opens 5pm daily (per Yelp); closing time not confirmed
Notes to Verify: Official website not confirmed. Dish specifics not pulled from a current menu. Opening year and owner from 2012 KQED/Grub Street coverage.

Directory Description: Iyasare is chef Shotaro Kamio's modern Japanese restaurant on Fourth Street. Kamio, formerly the chef at the beloved Yoshi's, opened it in late 2013 in the old O Chamé space at Fourth and Hearst. His cooking is refined yet approachable, drawing on the country cooking of northern Japan's Tohoku region alongside seasonal California ingredients. It serves lunch and dinner and has a pleasant patio, and it holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Highlights: Seasonal modern Japanese; Tohoku-inspired dishes; sake list; patio; lunch and dinner; Michelin Bib Gourmand
Notes to Verify: Website URL not confirmed in sources reached. Signature dishes not pulled from a current menu.

Directory Description: Tacubaya is a counter-service taqueria in the Fourth Street shopping district from Dona Savitsky, who created it as a casual sibling to her Temescal restaurant Doña Tomás. It has long been a go-to for handmade-tortilla tacos, chilaquiles and Mexican breakfast, with brunch served every day. Weekday happy hour and a relaxed dining room make it an easy stop while shopping on Fourth Street. It's recommended in the Michelin Guide.
Highlights: Tacos on handmade tortillas; daily brunch; weekday happy hour 2:30-6pm; counter service; Michelin Guide recommended
Notes to Verify: Moved into the former Pompette space on Fourth St around 2018. Signature dishes not pulled from a current menu.

Directory Description: Cha-Ya is a small, entirely vegan Japanese restaurant on Shattuck Avenue in North Berkeley. The menu covers plant-based takes on Japanese favorites, including sushi rolls, tempura, noodle soups and rice bowls, all without animal products. It's a longtime favorite with vegans and non-vegans alike, and the cozy room fills up quickly at dinner. Note that it's cash or Venmo only.
Highlights: 100% vegan menu; vegetable sushi rolls; tempura; noodle soups; cash or Venmo only
Notes to Verify: Dish list is general (from cuisine type); confirm signature items from current menu. Confirm days closed.

Directory Description: The Butcher's Son bills itself as California's original vegan butcher. Siblings Christina and Peter opened it in February 2016 after growing up working in their father's American diner, and they set out to recreate that nostalgic comfort food without animal products. Everything is plant-based, including faux meats and cheeses developed in-house, which star in hearty sandwiches like a chopped cheese, a Reuben and chicken parm. There's also a bakery case, some gluten-free options and a popular weekend brunch.
Highlights: House-made vegan meats and cheeses; chopped cheese; Reuben; chicken parm sandwich; bakery; weekend brunch; gluten-free options
Notes to Verify: Owners' last name not confirmed. Hours not captured.

Address: Fourth St, Berkeley, CA 94710 (street number not confirmed)
Directory Description: Oceanview Diner is a landmark neighborhood diner on Fourth Street serving breakfast classics with a twist, such as soufflé pancakes, along with omelets, waffles, house-made corned beef hash and a Philadelphia-style breakfast with scrapple. Later in the day it offers sandwiches like Reubens, tacos, salads and soups, plus beer and desserts. It also runs a gourmet deli counter and caters private events, and it ranks among Tripadvisor's top-rated Berkeley restaurants.
Highlights: Soufflé pancakes; house-made corned beef hash; Philadelphia breakfast with scrapple; Reubens; gourmet deli; catering and private events
Notes to Verify: Address, phone and hours could not be scraped; the address shown is unconfirmed. Owner and history unknown.

Cuisine: Indonesian/Southeast Asian bakery and coffee bar
Directory Description: Kopi Bar & Bakery is chef-owner Nora Haron's Indonesian-inspired cafe, which moved to Berkeley from Walnut Creek in fall 2025. Coffee drinks include playful avocado coffees, and the pastry case is filled with Southeast Asian flavors such as kaya toast brûlée. It quickly landed on Eater's list of the hottest new East Bay restaurants and was part of Berkeley Restaurant Week 2026.
Highlights: Avocado coffee; kaya toast brûlée; Indonesian-inspired pastries; specialty coffee
Notes to Verify: Exact street address and phone not found. Hours conflict between Berkeleyside (11-5) and website/Yelp (9-4 / 10-5).

Directory Description: Bar Panisse is the newer sibling of Chez Panisse, opened in December 2025 next door on Shattuck Avenue. Led by chef Amelia Telc, it carries the mothership's farm-to-table approach into a more casual bar setting, with small plates that change with the seasons, such as sage and anchovy fritters in winter or fried soft-shell crab with celery root remoulade in spring. The cocktails are polished takes on classics, including a gimlet with Meyer lemon cordial and a Sazerac.
Highlights: Seasonal small plates; sage and anchovy fritters; soft-shell crab with celery root remoulade; Meyer lemon gimlet; Sazerac; walk-in friendly bar
Notes to Verify: Phone is shared with Chez Panisse. Part of the Chez Panisse (Alice Waters) business.

Directory Description: Sichuan Style is a busy, well-loved spot on upper Solano Avenue for the bold, numbing heat of Sichuan cooking. Locals regularly name it among the best places to eat on Solano. The menu covers the classics, from mapo tofu and dry-fried green beans to spicy fish dishes and dan dan noodles, and it's open daily for lunch and dinner, with takeout available.
Highlights: Sichuan classics; mapo tofu; spicy fish; dan dan noodles; takeout
Notes to Verify: Dish list inferred from the cuisine; confirm against the current menu. Owners unknown.

Directory Description: Noor Indian Fusion Kitchen serves Indian cooking with a modern, fusion twist on University Avenue. It is one of the most highly rated Indian restaurants in the area on Yelp and OpenTable, and it serves both lunch and dinner. It also caters events of all sizes.
Highlights: Indian fusion dishes; lunch and dinner; catering
Notes to Verify: Website lists multiple locations; confirm whether Berkeley is the flagship and whether it's a local owner-run business. Signature dishes and owners not found.

Directory Description: Zaytoon has been serving Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cooking on Albany's Solano Avenue since June 2016, blending traditional recipes with a fresh, contemporary spin. The menu runs from mezze and ribeye kebabs to entrées like braised short ribs, pan-seared branzino, roasted lamb shank and Moroccan roasted chicken. Weekend brunch brings Turkish breakfast, Greek omelets and kataifi pancakes. There's a full bar with weekday happy hour, and it's one of the top-rated restaurants in Albany.
Highlights: Ribeye kebabs; lamb shank; Moroccan roasted chicken; pan-seared branzino; weekend brunch with Turkish breakfast and kataifi pancakes; full bar; happy hour
Hours: Lunch and dinner Tue-Sun; brunch Sat-Sun 11am-2:30pm; closed Mon
Notes to Verify: Owners not named on the pages reached ('Your Hosts' page not captured).

Directory Description: Bowl'd Korean Rice Bar is a Solano Avenue favorite for hearty Korean comfort food. The specialty is dolsot bibimbap, served sizzling in hot stone bowls so the rice crisps at the bottom, alongside Korean barbecue meats, stews and banchan. It's casual and family-friendly, open late for Solano, and consistently among Albany's highest-ranked restaurants.
Highlights: Dolsot (hot stone) bibimbap; Korean BBQ plates; stews; banchan; late hours
Hours: Daily from 11am; closing 9-11pm (Yelp and Instagram differ)
Notes to Verify: Hours conflict between sources. Owner not named. Has a sister location (bowldbbq.com lists Albany as one of its locations).

Directory Description: 5 Tacos and Beers is a family-owned taqueria from Lito Saldaña, whose family name also shows up on the house ale. It's known for organic ingredients and handmade corn tortillas, which make the menu naturally gluten-friendly, and for pairing tacos with local craft beer. Crispy tacos and traditional plates fill out the menu, and big party packs make it easy to feed a group. There's also a happy hour.
Highlights: Handmade corn tortillas; organic, gluten-friendly tacos; crispy tacos; local craft beer; taco party packs; happy hour
Hours: Mon, Wed, Thu, Sun 11am-8pm; Fri-Sat 11am-9pm (per website)
Notes to Verify: Small local group with more than one location. Albany location opened about 2022. Website hours skip Tuesday; Yelp shows Tue 11am-9pm.

Directory Description: Cugini Ristorante has been serving Italian cooking on Solano Avenue since 1996. The kitchen is known for handcrafted pizzas from its wood-fired oven, along with pastas and Italian classics. There's a bar, and the restaurant takes reservations and caters events.
Highlights: Wood-fired pizza; pastas; bar; reservations; catering
Notes to Verify: Owners and signature dishes not found (website pages were image-based). ZIP 94707 per Yelp even though listed as Albany; verify.

Directory Description: Everest Kitchen is a highly rated Himalayan restaurant on Albany's Solano Avenue, earning some of the strongest reviews on the street. The menu features Nepali favorites like momo dumplings alongside curries and tandoor dishes. It serves lunch and dinner, takes reservations, and offers online ordering for takeout.
Highlights: Momo; Nepali and Indian curries; tandoori dishes; reservations; online ordering
Notes to Verify: Owners and signature dishes not confirmed from a source; dish list is general.

Directory Description: Aangan is a popular Indian restaurant on San Pablo Avenue in Albany and a frequent recommendation among locals. The menu covers North Indian favorites, including curries, tandoori dishes and fresh-baked naan, with plenty of vegetarian options. It's open for lunch and dinner, with takeout available.
Highlights: North Indian curries; tandoori; naan; vegetarian options; lunch and dinner
Notes to Verify: Hours conflict between sources. Owner and signature dishes not found.

Cuisine: French pastry and Portuguese pastéis de nata
Directory Description: Pâtisserie Rotha is a small artisan French pastry shop on San Pablo Avenue that has drawn lines down the block since it opened in 2018, and it still sells out quickly. The case is filled with classic French pastries, brioche and crémeux, but the star is the Portuguese pastel de nata. It's open only a few mornings a week, so arrive early.
Highlights: Pastéis de nata; brioche; French pastries; sells out early
Notes to Verify: Bakery/takeout only, no full restaurant. Owner name not found.
